title: Memory leak when trying to free RID with RenderingServer.free_rid()
body:
### Tested versions

-Reproduceable in v4.4.beta1.official [d33da79d3]
-Reproduceable in v4.4.dev7.official [46c8f8c5c] 
-Reproduceable in v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Godot v4.4.beta1 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 threads)

### Issue description

I am creating a backbuffer for a `Compositor Effect` by calling` texture_create()` from the `RenderingDevice` and storing the resulting `RID` in a variable. When I detect a change in the size of the scene buffer, I attempt to free the `RID` of my texture and create a new one in a different size. Looking at the Windows task manager it seems memory isn't getting freed. Resizing the 3d viewport in the editor quickly racks up calls to my texture creation method and I can see memory usage rise, only freeing when the editor is closed.

In both the tested 4.4 versions, memory appears to be freed correctly in the Run Project popup window. It only affects the editor window.
In 4.3, the Run Project window is different and the leak is noticed there too. When I close the Run window, some memory is returned.

### Steps to reproduce

See MRP below

Resize the 3d viewport by scrubbing an window edge back and forth in the editor.
A notification is printed to the console every time the texture is freed and recreated.
For me, at time of testing, after around 100 calls I notice memory usage rise.

Run project
Resize preview window
Memory usage appears stable

[rid_test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18553772/rid_test.zip)
